caption_en:
1 Israeli = 16 Egyptians? 👥

Same region. Same sun. GDP per person (2024), and how many neighbours it takes to match one Israeli:

🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia: 1.5 ($35,528)
🇮🇶 Iraq: about 9 ($6,162)
🇱🇧 Lebanon: about 10 ($5,248)
🇯🇴 Jordan: about 11 ($5,081)
🇪🇬 Egypt: about 16 ($3,287)
🇸🇾 Syria: about 56 ($962, GDP 2022, latest)
🇾🇪 Yemen: about 273 ($199, IMF estimate)
🇮🇱 Israel: $54,213

Only Qatar makes more per person ($76,439). The UAE comes close ($52,880).

And it isn't oil. Natural resources bring in about 0.1% of Israel's economy. Iraq: 39.8%. Saudi Arabia: 24.8% (World Bank, 2019).

Israelis love to work, to build, to make something new every morning. But this isn't about people. Talent is everywhere. Most of this gap is war, and how countries are run. Income per person isn't happiness, and it isn't anyone's worth.

Send this to someone who thinks it's all about resources.

How we counted: each country's 2024 GDP in current US dollars divided by its 2024 population; ratio = Israel's figure divided by the country's.
Sources: GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook, Oct 2026 edition (2024 values; Yemen is an IMF estimate). Syria: World Bank, GDP 2022 (latest available). Population: World Bank, World Development Indicators, 2024. Natural resources: World Bank WDI, total natural resources rents, % of GDP, 2019 (Syria: no recent data). Map: Natural Earth.

Made with AI tools. AI voice.
caption_he:
ישראלי אחד מייצר בממוצע כמו 16 מצרים, 11 ירדנים, 10 לבנונים ו־273 תימנים (תמ"ג לנפש, 2024). רק קטאר עוקפת אותנו, והאמירויות קרובות. וזה לא נפט: משאבי טבע מכניסים כ־0.1% מהכלכלה הישראלית. ישראלים פשוט אוהבים לעבוד, לבנות ולייצר. אבל זה לא עניין של אנשים, כישרון יש בכל מקום. רוב הפער הוא מלחמה, ואיך מנהלים מדינות.
שלחו את זה למי שחושב שהכול זה משאבי טבע.
